summary: Old Mutual warned the public about fake videos, apparently made with AI, that imitated the face and voice of its chairman, a former finance minister, to push bogus investment schemes on social media. He publicly denied any involvement.
technical_summary: Scammers used deepfake video and cloned synthetic voice of a well-known financial figure in social media posts to solicit investments. The realistic likeness lent false credibility to fraudulent products, and victims were directed to unauthorised schemes.
deployers: Unknown scammers impersonating the Old Mutual chairman

sector.quote: An investment scam using a fake likeness of Trevor Manuel (pictured), the chairman of Old Mutual, is circulating on social media.

harm_type.quote: Too many people have lost their hard-earned money, especially what they've saved for later in life

notes: The quoted loss statement is a general warning by the impersonated figure, not a count of victims of these specific videos.

summary: Drivers in India said Uber's selfie-based identity check locked them out of their accounts after changes in appearance or in poor lighting, costing them work. Uber said deactivations are not based on facial recognition alone.
technical_summary: Uber's Real-Time ID Check compares a driver's live selfie to a stored photo using a cloud facial recognition service, and mismatches temporarily block accounts. False non-matches arise from facial hair, haircuts, lighting or low-quality cameras, and affected drivers report limited recourse.

sector.quote: Uber drivers in India say that problems with the facial recognition they use to access their apps is costing them work.

technology.quote: Uber checks that a driver's face matches what the company has on file through a program called "Real-Time ID Check."

failure_mode.quote: Many suspected that a change in their appearance, such as facial hair, a shaved head, or a haircut, was to blame.

harm_type.quote: Uber drivers in India say that problems with the facial recognition they use to access their apps is costing them work.

affected_population.quote: Uber drivers in India say that problems with the facial recognition they use to access their apps is costing them work.

notes: Uber disputes that facial recognition alone causes deactivations; one driver's case was attributed by Uber to guideline violations.

summary: A Kansas resident received text messages with fake nude images, apparently AI-generated, showing his face on another body in his own home. The sender threatened to send them to his Facebook contacts unless he paid money. He reported it to police.
technical_summary: Extortionists used generative image tools to composite a victim's face from social media onto synthetic nude images set in his home, then sent them with screenshots of his friends list to coerce payment. The imagery was fake but plausible enough to threaten reputation and employment.

technology.quote: Criminals use AI to generate nude photos of people, and then threaten to send them to friends and family unless you send them money.

failure_mode.quote: Criminals use AI to generate nude photos of people, and then threaten to send them to friends and family unless you send them money.

harm_type.quote: It's scary to think if this made its way to my boss, or if this made its way to my family

notes: No payment is reported; the target recognized the images as fake and blocked the numbers.

summary: A man in his sixties developed bromide poisoning and was hospitalized after replacing table salt with sodium bromide, following a ChatGPT conversation about removing chloride from his diet. Doctors could not obtain his chat log.
technical_summary: A user asked ChatGPT about substituting chloride in his diet and later ingested sodium bromide for three months. When the case authors asked a similar question, the chatbot also listed bromide without a health warning or asking about the purpose, indicating missing safety context in health advice.

technology.quote: after consulting the artificial intelligence--based conversational large language model, ChatGPT, for health information

failure_mode.quote: the response also included bromide, did not provide a specific health warning

harm_type.quote: a 60-year-old man developed bromism, also known as bromide toxicity, after consulting ChatGPT
Doctors detail how a man experienced poison-caused psychosis after he followed AI-guided dietary advice.

notes: Authors could not access the original conversation, so the exact advice given is unverified.

summary: Uruguay's state utility warned of a manipulated video in which a famous footballer's image and voice were altered to endorse a fake investment scheme. The scam led to phishing sites that collected personal and payment data.
technical_summary: Scammers used AI to alter a news-report video and a footballer's face and voice so he appeared to recommend a fake investment platform, then ran paid social media ads leading to phishing pages imitating the utility and government bodies to harvest personal and payment details.

technology.quote: La imagen y la voz de Suárez están alteradas para hacerle decir al futbolista que la inversión es una buena idea

failure_mode.quote: La imagen y la voz de Suárez están alteradas para hacerle decir al futbolista que la inversión es una buena idea

harm_type.quote: una clara maniobra de phishing, a través del cual los estafadores obtienen datos personales y medios de pago

notes: No confirmed victim losses are reported in the excerpts.

summary: The New York Times sued OpenAI and Microsoft, alleging that millions of its articles were used without permission to train AI chatbots that now compete with it, and that some outputs reproduce its articles word for word.
technical_summary: Large language models behind ChatGPT were allegedly trained on scraped copyrighted news articles without licence or payment. The complaint cites examples of GPT-4 outputting articles verbatim, claims the resulting products substitute for the publisher, and seeks damages and destruction of models trained on its content.

sector.quote: The New York Times sued OpenAI and Microsoft for copyright infringement on Wednesday

technology.quote: millions of articles published by The Times were used to train automated chatbots

failure_mode.quote: millions of articles published by The Times were used to train automated chatbots

notes: Allegations from a lawsuit; the defendants maintain fair use and the case had not been decided at the time of the reports.

summary: A Tesla Model Y that its driver said was using Autopilot hit a parked Michigan State Police car that had its emergency lights on. No one was injured, and federal regulators opened an investigation.
technical_summary: A Tesla driver-assistance system reportedly engaged on a highway failed to avoid a stationary police vehicle partly in a lane with flashing lights. The case fits a pattern of Autopilot crashes into stopped emergency vehicles, linked to perception limits and inadequate driver-attention monitoring.

technology.quote: a Model Y that was reportedly operating in Autopilot struck a stationary police car early Wednesday morning in Michigan

failure_mode.quote: criticized by the National Transportation Safety Board for failing to adequately monitor drivers to make sure they are paying attention

severity.quote: Nobody was injured in the crash.

notes: The driver also received citations for failure to move over and driving with a suspended license; Autopilot use was driver-reported.

summary: An empty Waymo robotaxi drove into a flooded road in San Antonio and was swept into a creek. No one was hurt. Waymo recalled its software across thousands of vehicles and paused service in some areas.
technical_summary: Waymo's driving system detected possible untraversable floodwater on a 40 mph road but slowed rather than stopped and entered the flooded lane. The company's filing identified a software limitation on higher-speed roads, leading to a recall, map updates and tighter weather operating constraints.

technology.quote: Waymo is recalling 3,791 vehicles after one of the company's driverless cars was washed away during flash flooding in San Antonio

failure_mode.quote: The Waymo AV detected potentially untraversable flood water and proceeded at reduced speed

harm_type.quote: Waymo lost one of its driverless cars on April 20 after it entered a flooded lane near Salado Creek

severity.quote: There were no passengers and no one was injured, according to Bonelli.

notes: A similar later incident in Atlanta is mentioned in another report but is not coded here.

summary: A former First Lady of Namibia warned that scammers were using AI-manipulated videos and cloned voice calls of her to promote fake forex schemes. Her office said there were many victims, including a woman who lost her retirement savings.
technical_summary: Fraudsters built fake social media accounts and used manipulated video, with her genuine footage dubbed with a voice resembling hers, plus synthetic video calls, to solicit investments with local bank details. The realistic likeness of a public figure made the schemes more convincing and widespread across platforms.

technology.quote: The TikTok clips have used genuine footage of Mrs Geingos speaking dubbed with a voice that sounds like hers.
The latest, according to Geingos, includes AI manipulated videos of her asking members of the public to invest in fraudulent schemes.

failure_mode.quote: fraudsters are using her name and likeness to target unsuspecting citizens

harm_type.quote: one woman who was swindled out of her retirement savings

summary: Police in Sichuan, China publicized ten cases in which people used AI tools to fabricate news of disasters, accidents and other incidents to gain online traffic and income. Authorities imposed administrative penalties on those responsible.
technical_summary: Individuals used text and image generation software, in one case a custom tool producing hundreds of thousands of articles through volunteer-run accounts, to fabricate or alter news stories such as landslides, earthquakes and accidents. Low cost and automation let false reports spread widely for engagement and platform payouts.
systems: AI text and image generation tools
notes: Source excerpt is in Chinese, so all tags are marked inferred rather than quoted.

summary: Amazon Web Services had a roughly 13-hour interruption to one service in mainland China after its AI coding tool Kiro reportedly chose to delete and recreate part of its environment. Amazon said it was user error and misconfigured access controls, not AI.
technical_summary: Kiro, an agentic coding tool that normally needs two human approvals, ran with its operator's broader permissions and reportedly deleted and recreated the environment it was working on, causing the outage. Amazon attributes the event to access-control misconfiguration; the dispute concerns whether autonomy or permissions was the root cause.

technology.quote: Kiro is an agentic tool, meaning it can take autonomous actions on behalf of users.

failure_mode.quote: the bot had the permissions of its operator, and a human error there allowed more access than expected.

harm_type.quote: Amazon Web Services suffered a 13-hour outage to one system in December

notes: Causation is disputed: reporting attributes it to the AI agent, Amazon to human error and permissions.

summary: A fabricated freelance journalist persona, using AI-assisted writing and an AI-generated headshot, published opinion pieces in several Canadian outlets before publishers could not verify the identity and removed the articles. One report alleges the pieces targeted Moroccan dissidents.
technical_summary: A non-existent contributor used AI tools to produce articles and a synthetic profile image, built credibility through accumulated bylines, and passed editorial vetting that relied on email contact and prior publications. Outlets could not verify identity or credentials and have since tightened contributor verification.

sector.quote: an artificially generated persona operating under this name successfully infiltrated several prominent Canadian news outlets and policy hubs

technology.quote: The phantom writer leveraged AI tools to bypass established editorial vetting

failure_mode.quote: The phantom writer leveraged AI tools to bypass established editorial vetting, publishing dozens of articles that pushed hyper-specific foreign policy narratives.

harm_type.quote: we are unable to verify he is who he claimed to be.

notes: The persona's motives and the targeting allegation come from a single outlet's report and are not independently confirmed.
